entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Pittichová et al. (2008), AJ 136, 1127); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Giacobini–Zinner was the first comet visited by a spacecraft, when ICE passed through its tail in 1985. Its dust also feeds the Draconid meteor shower. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Pittichová et al. (2008), AJ 136, 1127: effective radius 1.82 km ± 0.05. No axis ratio is published; a sphere is displayed. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
